title: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
summary: Procedure established by law under Article 21 does not mean due process of law (as under the US Constitution). Each fundamental right is a separate guarantee and must be read independently. Overruled in substance by Maneka Gandhi v. UOI.

title: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
summary: Overruled — habeas corpus cannot be suspended during emergency.

title: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib Sehravardi
summary: Test for determining "other authority" under Article 12 (definition of State). A body is an "other authority" if: (i) the entire share capital is held by the State; (ii) the State has deep and pervasive control; (iii) the functions are of public importance; (iv) government is the largest single shareholder.

title: Amazon.Com NV Investment Holdings LLC v. Future Retail Ltd.
summary: Emergency arbitrator award has legal sanctity; interim order of emergency arbitrator can be enforced under Section 17(2) of the Arbitration Act. Parties cannot circumvent arbitration agreements through parallel proceedings.

title: Amit Kapil v. State of Haryana
summary: High Court in revision under CrPC §397 (BNSS §438) can interfere when the lower court has not applied judicial mind to material on record, has failed to record reasons for the order passed, or has acted arbitrarily. Failure to consider material evidence constitutes material irregularity.

title: Arcelor Mittal India v. Satish Kumar Gupta
summary: Section 29A eligibility for resolution applicants.

title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
summary: Arrest must be the last resort. Police must apply their mind and be satisfied of the necessity of arrest. Mechanical or routine arrest without recording reasons and without examining whether necessity conditions are met is impermissible. Magistrates must not authorise remand mechanically. Applicable to challenge the necessity and documentation of an arrest.
holding: Arrest must be the last resort, not the first option. Police must satisfy themselves of the necessity of arrest before arresting in offences punishable up to 7 years. Mechanical arrest without application of mind is impermissible.
titleAliases: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar

title: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India
summary: SC directed Election Commission to require candidates for elections to disclose their criminal antecedents, educational qualifications, and personal assets at the time of filing nomination papers. Right of voters to know candidates' backgrounds held to be a fundamental right.

title: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
summary: Writ of mandamus and PIL under Article 32: fundamental rights of weaker sections can be enforced through PIL; court can take cognisance of letters and communications. State has positive obligation to ensure fundamental rights are not violated by its agencies.

title: Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa
summary: Wide definition of industry under ID Act.

title: Bayer Corporation v Natco Pharma Ltd
summary: First compulsory licence under Patents Act §84 for Bayer's Nexavar, establishing the framework for public interest licensing of patented pharmaceuticals.
holding: Compulsory licence may be granted where the patented invention is not available to the public at a reasonably affordable price and is not worked in India.

title: Bharat Aluminium Co. v. Kaiser Aluminium Technical Service
summary: Constitution Bench: Part I of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act 1996 applies only when the seat of arbitration is in India. Courts in India cannot intervene in foreign-seated arbitrations except as permitted by Part II. Overruled Bhatia International.
titleAliases: Bharat Aluminium Co. v. Kaiser Aluminium Technical Service

title: Bharathi Knitting Co. v. DHL Worldwide Express
summary: Courier service and CPA applicability.

title: Bhatia International v. Bulk Trading S.A.
summary: Note: Superseded by Bharat Aluminium (BALCO) on seat theory. Part I of Arbitration Act applies only when seat is India. Historical context: courts had expansive jurisdiction over foreign-seated arbitrations pre-BALCO.

title: Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena
summary: Courts must address maintenance applications without procrastination; the object of maintenance is to prevent vagrancy and destitution of the wife and children. The husband has a duty to disclose his income truthfully; if he fails to do so the court can draw adverse inference and assess maintenance on a higher estimate of income.

title: Bibi Zubaida Khatoon v. Nawab Mohd. Ali Khan
summary: Adverse possession requires: (a) open and continuous possession, (b) hostile possession (without title), (c) for a period of 12 years (Limitation Act), (d) with intent to possess as owner. All three elements must coexist.

title: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
summary: Right to free speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) includes the right to remain silent. Standing respectfully during the national anthem without singing constitutes proper respect; the State cannot compel citizens to sing. Expulsion of children who stood silently violated their fundamental rights.

title: Bir Singh v. Mukesh Kumar
summary: Legality of blank cheques and presumption under s.139.

title: Booz Allen & Hamilton Inc. v. SBI Home Finance Ltd.
summary: Courts may grant interim relief under Section 9 of the Arbitration Act when arbitral proceedings are contemplated or pending.
holding: Courts may grant interim relief under Section 9 of the Arbitration Act when arbitral proceedings are contemplated or pending.

title: Central Bureau of Investigation v. Maninder Singh
summary: CBI investigation and sanction requirements.

title: Central Inland Water Transport Corporation v. Brojo Nath Ganguly
summary: Termination clauses allowing termination by notice alone, without assigning reasons, in public employment contracts are unconscionable and void as against public policy. Concept of natural justice applies to employment termination by public employers.
titleAliases: Central Inland Water Transport Corporation v. Brojo Nath Ganguly

title: Chaturbhuj v. Sita Bai
summary: Maintenance under CrPC §125 is intended to prevent destitution; "unable to maintain herself" means the respondent's own income and means are insufficient relative to the standard of living enjoyed during the marriage. Husband's income is the primary yardstick; the court must look at actual income, not mere capacity to earn. Existing liabilities and dependants of the husband must be considered.
titleAliases: Chaturbhuj v. Sita Bai

title: Cheran Properties Ltd. v. Kasturi and Sons Ltd.
summary: A non-signatory to an arbitration agreement may in certain circumstances be bound by it. Group of companies doctrine: arbitration agreement between two or more parties may operate to bind other parties where the non-signatory's relationship with a signatory, commonality of subject matter, and composite nature of the transaction indicate mutual intent. Section 35 of the Arbitration Act binds "persons claiming under" a party.
holding: Non-signatory bound by arbitration award where non-signatory claims under a party and circumstances reveal common intent to arbitrate; group of companies doctrine applied.

title: CIT v. B.C. Srinivasa Setty
summary: Capital gains — goodwill computation.

title: CIT v. Calcutta Knitwears
summary: Penny stock and bogus LTCG.

title: CIT v. Sun Engineering Works
summary: Reopening assessment — tangible material required.

title: CIT v. Walfort Share and Stock Brokers
summary: Transfer pricing and disallowance.

title: Commissioner of Income Tax v. Brij Lal
summary: Search and seizure — block assessment.

title: Common Cause (A Regd. Society) v. Union of India
summary: Right to die with dignity is a fundamental right under Article 21. Passive euthanasia is constitutionally permissible. Active euthanasia is not. Advance directives (living will) are legally valid. Process for implementation of advance directives laid down.

title: Common Cause v. Union of India
summary: High Courts may entertain public interest writs where executive action affects public rights. Locus standi is relaxed in PIL matters.
holding: High Courts may entertain public interest writs where executive action affects public rights. Locus standi is relaxed in PIL matters.

title: D. Stephens v. Nosibolla
summary: Revisional jurisdiction is supervisory in nature; the High Court can interfere if the lower court has exercised its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity. Revision is not a second appeal; the court should not reappraise evidence unless the lower court has acted perversely.

title: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar
summary: Re-promulgation of ordinances from time to time is a subversion of democratic processes and a fraud on the Constitution. Ordinance-making power under Articles 123 and 213 is meant to meet extraordinary situations, not to bypass the Legislature indefinitely.

title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
summary: Mandatory guidelines for arrest and detention: (1) arresting officer must bear visible identification; (2) arrest memo must be prepared at the time of arrest, attested by a family member or respectable person, and countersigned by the arrested person; (3) grounds of arrest must be communicated; (4) a relative or friend must be informed of the arrest and place of custody; (5) arrested person must be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours. Violation of these guidelines entitles the victim to compensation as a public-law remedy under Articles 21 and 226.
holding: Mandatory guidelines on arrest procedure to prevent custodial violence; violation is actionable and may ground contempt of court.
titleAliases: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal

title: D.K. Jain v. National Insurance Co.
summary: Insurance claim delay as deficiency in service.

title: Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh
summary: Temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rule 1 CPC requires: (i) prima facie case, (ii) balance of convenience, and (iii) irreparable injury. All three conditions must be satisfied; mere apprehension of loss is insufficient.
holding: All three elements — prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable injury — must be satisfied for a temporary injunction.
titleAliases: Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh

title: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra
summary: Jurisdiction for NI Act §138 complaints lies only at the court where the cheque was dishonoured (i.e., where the drawee bank is located). The payee's place of business or residence does not confer jurisdiction. This ruling was prospective; Parliament later amended NI Act to expand territorial jurisdiction.
titleAliases: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra

title: Dattatreya Shanker Mote v. Anand Chintaman Datar
summary: Specific performance — readiness and willingness.

title: Dayawati v. Yogesh Kumar Gosain
summary: Arbitration of NI Act disputes — Delhi HC.

title: Delhi High Court Bar Association v. Delhi High Court
summary: Section 9 interim relief: courts must satisfy themselves on balance of convenience and irreparable harm before granting interim relief. Arbitral tribunal must be appointed and given opportunity to pass interim orders before Section 9 Court entertains further applications, unless tribunal cannot effectively pass orders.

title: Delhi Transport Corporation v. D.T.C. Mazdoor Congress
summary: Termination of permanent employees of statutory bodies without inquiry and without assigning reasons violates Article 21. Right to livelihood is part of right to life. Service jurisprudence requires natural justice before termination of substantive government employment.

title: Deputy Commissioner and Special Land Acquisition Officer v. M/S S.V. Global Mill Limited
summary: Consolidated judgment (consolidating ~100 connected matters) on land acquisition under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR Act) and the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Interpretation of Section 24 of the 2013 Act: where no award under S.11 of the 1894 Act has been made, all provisions of the 2013 Act relating to determination of compensation apply. The 2013 Act is a beneficial legislation to be construed purposively. Rehabilitation and resettlement entitlements under the 2013 Act do not apply retrospectively under S.24(1)(a). Judgment dated 9 February 2026.
holding: Section 24(1)(a) RFCTLARR Act 2013: all compensation-related provisions of the 2013 Act apply where no award under S.11 of 1894 Act has been passed; however rehabilitation and resettlement benefits cannot be extended retrospectively.

title: Dharma Prathishthanam v. Madhok Construction
summary: Development agreement and specific performance.

title: E.I.D. Parry (India) Ltd. v. Panchaiyappa
summary: Commercial purpose exclusion from CPA.

title: ECI SPIC and Oxo Biotech v. State of Haryana
summary: Security cheque defence limitations.

title: Embassy Property v. State of Karnataka
summary: Stamp duty on amalgamation schemes.

title: Essar Steel India Ltd. v. Satish Kumar Gupta
summary: Committee of Creditors primacy in resolution plan approval.
titleAliases: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel v. Satish Kumar Gupta

title: Garware Wall Ropes v. Coastal Marine Constructions
summary: Unstamped agreement — arbitration agreement validity.

title: Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh
summary: Compensation for mental agony, harassment, and loss of opportunity is justified in consumer disputes. Consumer courts are not restricted to refund; they can award interest and solatium. Unreasonable delay in refund itself constitutes deficiency in service.
holding: Compensation for mental agony and harassment is justified in consumer disputes. Consumer courts are not restricted to refund; they can award interest and solatium.
titleAliases: Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh

title: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
summary: Right to life under Article 21 is inconsistent with a right to die. Right to life includes right to live with human dignity up to natural death. May include "death with dignity" but not artificial termination of life. Overruled P. Rathinam v. UOI.

title: Glenmark Life Sciences Ltd. v. M/s Terminalia Arjuna
summary: IBC operational creditor rights.

title: Goa Plast (P) Ltd. v. Chico Ursula D'Souza
summary: Notice under s.138 — service requirements.

title: Gojer Brothers v. Union of India
summary: GST transition and input tax credit.

title: Golak Nath v. State of Punjab
summary: Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights. Under Article 13(2), "law" includes a constitutional amendment. Doctrine of prospective overruling introduced. Overruled by Keshvananda Bharti.

title: Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India
summary: Constitution Bench: Lieutenant Governor of NCT of Delhi is bound by the aid and advice of the elected Council of Ministers except in matters of land, police and public order. Real power must vest in elected representatives. The words "any matter" in the proviso to Article 239AA(4) cannot mean "every matter".

title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab
summary: Constitution Bench: Anticipatory bail under CrPC §438 is a device to secure personal liberty of persons falsely implicated or apprehending arrest on false charges. The power should be exercised with care and circumspection; court must consider the nature of accusation, antecedents, and likely misuse.
titleAliases: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab

title: Gurcharan Singh v. State (Delhi Administration)
summary: Bail considerations under CrPC §437/§439 (BNSS §479/§480): the court must weigh the seriousness of the accusation, the possibility of absconsion, the antecedents of the accused, and whether a prima facie case is made out. Bail is not to be withheld as a form of punishment.
holding: Bail considerations under CrPC §437/§439 (BNSS §480/§483): seriousness of accusation, possibility of absconsion, antecedents, prima facie case. Bail is not to be withheld as a form of punishment.
titleAliases: Gurcharan Singh v. State (Delhi Administration)

title: Himani Alloys v. Tata Steel
summary: Arbitration clause in unstamped agreement.

title: Hindustan Tin Works v. Employees
summary: Retrenchment compensation under ID Act.

title: HUDA v. Bhagwan Sahai
summary: Housing authority as service provider.

title: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
summary: Ninth Schedule laws enacted after Kesavananda Bharati (24 April 1973) are subject to judicial review. Two-fold test: whether the law violates fundamental rights AND whether that violation amounts to damage to the basic structure. If yes on both counts, the law can be struck down.

title: In Re: Order dated 17.03.2025 in Criminal Revision No. 1449/2024 (Suo Motu Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 1 of 2025)
summary: SC set aside HC (Allahabad) finding that accused only "prepared" and had not "attempted" rape of a minor. Prima facie case of attempt to rape established on the facts. Distinction between preparation and attempt explained: attempt begins where preparation ends and mens rea starts to be executed. SC directed National Judicial Academy to constitute expert committee to draft comprehensive guidelines on judicial sensitivity and compassion in sexual offence and vulnerable victim cases. Judgment dated 10 February 2026.
holding: HC finding of mere preparation (not attempt) to commit rape reversed; original summons under S.376 IPC r/w S.18 POCSO Act restored. NJA directed to frame sensitivity guidelines.

title: In Re: Presidential Reference (Third Judges Case)
summary: Third Judges Case. Collegium means CJI plus four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court for Supreme Court appointments. Clarified and expanded the collegium system. Individual opinion of CJI alone is not determinative.

title: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha
summary: Medical services fall under CPA unless gratuitous.

title: Indian Young Lawyers Assn. v. State of Kerala
summary: Sabarimala — religious denomination and Article 25.

title: Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala
summary: Sabarimala case. Exclusion of women of menstruating age (10–50 years) from the Sabarimala temple declared unconstitutional as violating Articles 14, 15, 17, and 25(1). Devotees of Lord Ayyappa do not constitute a separate religious denomination protected under Article 26. The prohibition based on notions of impurity (menstruation) is a form of untouchability.

title: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain
summary: 39th Amendment (Article 329A) which removed the election dispute of the Prime Minister from jurisdiction of courts declared unconstitutional as violative of the basic structure. Democracy and free and fair elections are part of the basic structure.

title: Indira Sawhney v. Union of India
summary: Mandal Commission case. 27% reservation for OBCs in public services upheld. Reservation in promotion not permissible under Article 16(4) (diluted by 77th Amendment). Total reservation cannot exceed 50% (50% ceiling rule). Creamy layer test applies to OBCs but not to SCs/STs. Caste is the predominant but not sole criterion for backwardness. Carry-forward rule for vacancies not permissible.
holding: OBC reservation at 27% upheld; 50% ceiling on total reservation; creamy layer excludes advanced OBC members; reservation in promotion impermissible.

title: Indira Sawhney v. Union of India
summary: Mandal commission — 50% cap on reservations.

title: Innoventive Industries Ltd. v. ICICI Bank
summary: Moratorium under IBC and overriding effect.

title: Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
summary: M. Nagaraj held per incuriam to the extent it requires the State to demonstrate quantifiable data on backwardness of SC/ST candidates for reservation in promotion — Indira Sawhney had already settled that no such data is required for SCs/STs. State still must show inadequacy of representation and efficiency.

title: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP
summary: No arrest can be made merely because it is lawful for the police officer to do so. Arrest is a serious matter affecting personal liberty. The arrestee must be informed of the grounds of arrest. A relative or friend of the arrested person must be informed of the arrest and the place of detention. The right to be informed of the grounds of arrest flows from Article 22(1) of the Constitution.

title: Jordan Diengdeh v. S.S. Chopra
summary: Irretrievable breakdown — need for law reform.

title: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
summary: Section 497 IPC (adultery) and Section 198(2) CrPC struck down as unconstitutional. Section 497 treated women as chattel of their husbands; it was manifestly arbitrary and violated Articles 14, 15, and 21. The husband's exclusive right to prosecute his wife's lover is a codified rule of patriarchy.

title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
summary: Landmark nine-judge bench: Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 (and Articles 14, 19). Privacy encompasses individual autonomy, dignity, and freedom. State may impose reasonable restrictions only if they satisfy a threefold test: legality, legitimate aim, proportionality. Overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh insofar as they denied right to privacy.
holding: Right to privacy is intrinsic to life and liberty under Article 21; legitimate State interference requires legality, legitimate aim, and proportionality.

title: K. Narendra v. Ravindra
summary: Joint family property and partition.

title: K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A. Deepa
summary: False criminal complaints filed by one spouse against the other constitute mental cruelty justifying divorce. Filing of multiple complaints, FIRs, and proceedings by wife to harass and humiliate husband amounts to cruelty within §13(1)(ia) HMA.

title: K. Veeraswami v. Union of India
summary: No FIR can be registered against a sitting High Court or Supreme Court judge for offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act without prior consultation with the Chief Justice of India and consent of the CJI. Judicial independence requires this protection.

title: K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan
summary: Specific performance is discretionary, not a matter of right. Court considers hardship to defendant, conduct of parties, and whether monetary compensation is adequate relief before granting specific performance of immovable property.
holding: Specific performance is discretionary, not a matter of right. Court considers hardship to defendant, conduct of parties, and whether monetary compensation is adequate relief before granting specific performance of immovable property.
titleAliases: K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan

title: Kalyan Dey Chowdhury v. Rita Dey Chowdhury
summary: The Supreme Court approved fixing maintenance at approximately 25% of the husband's net salary as a general benchmark where income is modest. Maintenance is not a punishment; it is a civil right. Quantum must be reasonable — neither illusory nor punitive. The court must apply its mind to the material on record.
titleAliases: Kalyan Dey Chowdhury v. Rita Dey Chowdhury

title: Kandla Export Corporation v. M/s OCI Corporation
summary: Appeals against enforcement of foreign arbitral awards lie only under Section 50 of the Arbitration Act, not under Section 13(1) of the Commercial Courts Act. Where Section 50 does not provide an appeal (e.g. when the enforcement petition succeeds), no separate right of appeal arises under the Commercial Courts Act. Legislative policy is to speedily enforce foreign awards.
holding: Appellate remedy against foreign award enforcement decisions is governed exclusively by S.50 of the Arbitration Act; Commercial Courts Act does not create additional appeal rights.

title: Kanu Sanyal v. District Magistrate
summary: Habeas corpus petition does not necessarily require physical production of the body; the court may in appropriate cases examine legality of detention on affidavits. The inquiry in habeas corpus is into the legality of the detention. Article 226 confers wide jurisdiction on High Courts to issue habeas corpus to any authority within territorial jurisdiction.

title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
summary: Landmark Constitution Bench (13 judges): Parliament can amend any provision of the Constitution including Fundamental Rights, but cannot alter or destroy the basic structure or essential features of the Constitution. Doctrine of basic structure laid down. Part of Article 31C which barred judicial review struck down. Overruled Golak Nath.
holding: Basic structure doctrine: Parliament's constituent power is subject to an implied limitation that the basic structure of the Constitution cannot be abrogated.

title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
summary: Established the basic structure doctrine — Parliament cannot amend the Constitution in a manner that destroys its basic features such as democracy, secularism, and judicial review.
holding: Parliament's amending power under Article 368 does not extend to altering the basic structure or framework of the Constitution.
titleAliases: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala

title: Kiran Singh v. Chaman Paswan
summary: A decree passed by a court without jurisdiction is a nullity and cannot be enforced. Title disputes in civil courts go to the court of competent territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction. Consent cannot confer jurisdiction that a court does not possess.

title: Krishnan v. Krishnaveni
summary: In the exercise of revisional jurisdiction the High Court can examine the legality and propriety of the order. Interference is warranted when the court below has acted in excess of jurisdiction, or has failed to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, or has acted perversely in the face of material evidence on record.

title: Kusum Ingots & Alloys Ltd. v. Pennar Peterson Securities Ltd.
summary: NI Act §138 creates a statutory presumption of liability; once the complainant proves issuance of cheque and dishonour, the burden shifts to the accused to rebut the presumption of debt or liability. The accused must prove by preponderance of probabilities that there was no existing debt.
titleAliases: Kusum Ingots & Alloys Ltd. v. Pennar Peterson Securities Ltd.

title: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India
summary: Judicial review is part of the basic structure of the Constitution. Clauses 323A(2)(d) and 323B(3)(d) of the Constitution which barred High Court jurisdiction over administrative and other tribunals struck down. High Courts' power of judicial review cannot be excluded.

title: L. Robert D'Souza v. Executive Engineer
summary: Temporary worker rights and termination.

title: Lakshmi Precision Screws Ltd. v. Ram Bhagwan
summary: Termination without enquiry or violation of principles of natural justice may warrant reinstatement or compensation in industrial disputes.
holding: Termination without enquiry or violation of principles of natural justice may warrant reinstatement or compensation in industrial disputes.

title: Laxmi Dyechem v. State of Gujarat
summary: Stop-payment instruction on a cheque issued for discharge of a legally enforceable debt attracts NI Act §138 liability. The drawer cannot defeat the statutory presumption simply by issuing a stop-payment instruction. The drawer must rebut the presumption of debt by cogent evidence.
titleAliases: Laxmi Dyechem v. State of Gujarat

title: Laxmi Engineering Works v. P.S.G. Industrial Institute
summary: Who is a consumer under CPA.

title: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
summary: Section 8(4) of the Representation of People Act 1951 which allowed convicted MPs/MLAs to remain in office pending appeal struck down as unconstitutional. On conviction by a court for an offence with sentence of two years or more, the member's seat is vacated immediately.

title: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
summary: Article 136 confers a discretionary jurisdiction on the Supreme Court to grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, order, or sentence of any court or tribunal. The power is exceptional and is exercised sparingly when substantial question of law of general importance is involved, or when the judgment is manifestly unjust.
holding: Deficiency in service includes delay, substandard performance, and failure to provide promised amenities. Consumer courts have jurisdiction over public bodies. Compensation can be awarded for mental agony beyond refund.
titleAliases: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
Khoday Distilleries Ltd. v. Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha

title: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
summary: Reservation in promotion for SC/ST employees permissible under Article 16(4A) if the State demonstrates: (a) backwardness; (b) inadequacy of representation; (c) overall administrative efficiency is maintained. Held per incuriam to the extent it requires demonstrating backwardness for SCs/STs (overruled on that point by Jarnail Singh).

title: M. Siddiq v. Mahant Suresh Das
summary: Ayodhya title dispute — possession and trust.

title: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
summary: Oleum gas leak case. Laid down the rule of Absolute Liability: an enterprise engaged in hazardous activity owes an absolute and non-delegable duty to compensate for harm caused. Unlike the rule in Rylands v. Fletcher, no exceptions are available. Size of enterprise determines quantum of damages.
holding: Absolute liability (non-delegable, no exceptions) applies to enterprises carrying on hazardous activities causing harm to others.

title: M/S Emaar MGF Land Ltd. v. Aftab Singh
summary: An arbitration clause in a Buyer's Agreement between a real estate developer and a home buyer cannot circumscribe the jurisdiction of a Consumer Forum under the Consumer Protection Act 1986, notwithstanding the 2015 amendment to Section 8 of the Arbitration Act. Consumer disputes arising from housing projects are not arbitrable; Consumer Forums are constituted to serve a specific public purpose.
holding: Arbitration clause does not oust Consumer Forum jurisdiction; consumer disputes under housing/real estate projects are non-arbitrable.

title: Maksud Saiyed v. State of Gujarat
summary: Quashing when dispute is essentially civil in nature.

title: Management of M/s. Panipat Woollen v. Bhag Singh
summary: Termination of probationer — principles.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
summary: Landmark: procedure established by law under Article 21 must be just, fair, and reasonable (i.e. must satisfy due process of law). Fundamental rights are not isolated silos; Articles 14, 19, and 21 form a golden triangle and must be read together. Right to travel abroad is a facet of Article 21. Overruled AK Gopalan to the extent of compartmentalisation.
holding: Article 21 requires procedure that is just, fair and reasonable; Articles 14, 19 and 21 are inter-connected and cannot be read in isolation.
titleAliases: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
summary: Article 21 protects personal liberty; procedure established by law must be fair, just, and reasonable. Writ jurisdiction is available for violation of fundamental rights.
holding: Article 21 protects personal liberty; procedure established by law must be fair, just, and reasonable. Writ jurisdiction is available for violation of fundamental rights.
titleAliases: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v Union of India

title: McDowell & Co. v. CTO
summary: Tax planning vs tax evasion distinction.

title: Meters and Instruments Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanchan Mehta
summary: Cheque dishonour case can be summarily tried and compounded at any stage. Court must promote settlement in NI Act cases. Compensation under §357 CrPC can be directed to be paid in lieu of fine. Accused who pays cheque amount plus reasonable compensation is entitled to acquittal.
titleAliases: Meters and Instruments Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanchan Mehta

title: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
summary: Articles 368(4) and 368(5) (inserted by 42nd Amendment) which placed constitutional amendments beyond judicial review struck down as violative of the basic structure. Part of Article 31C which gave primacy to all Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights also struck down. Harmony between DPSPs and Fundamental Rights is itself a basic structure element.

title: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
summary: Basic structure — Articles 14 and 19 part of basic structure.

title: Modi Cements Ltd. v. Kuchil Kumar Nandi
summary: Stop payment and legally enforceable debt.

title: Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das
summary: Interim relief must not be granted without hearing the opposite party except in exceptional cases of extreme urgency. Ex parte injunction requires the court to record reasons for urgency.

title: N. Srinivasa v. Kuttukaran Machine Tools Ltd.
summary: Plaintiff seeking specific performance must prove readiness and willingness to perform their part of the contract throughout. Mere readiness at the time of suit is insufficient if conduct shows unwillingness.
holding: Plaintiff seeking specific performance must prove readiness and willingness to perform their part of the contract throughout. Mere readiness at the time of suit is insufficient if conduct shows unwillingness.
titleAliases: N. Srinivasa v. Kuttukaran Machine Tools Ltd.

title: N.V. Narendranath v. Chairman, CAAB
summary: Article 136 jurisdiction is not a regular avenue of appeal. SC will not interfere merely because another view is possible. Interference is warranted when there is illegality, perversity, grave miscarriage of justice, or where question of law of general importance requires authoritative pronouncement.

title: Nahar Industrial Enterprises v. Hong Kong Shanghai Banking
summary: Mortgage and enforcement of security interest.

title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nitin Khandelwal
summary: Repudiation of insurance claim without proper investigation amounts to deficiency in service under Consumer Protection Act. Insurer cannot repudiate on grounds of breach of condition unless breach is so fundamental as to go to the root of the contract. Consumer forum has power to award compensation for wrongful repudiation.
holding: Repudiation of insurance claim without proper investigation amounts to deficiency in service. Insurer cannot repudiate unless breach is fundamental. Consumer forum may award compensation for wrongful repudiation.
titleAliases: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nitin Khandelwal

title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Prithvi Chand
summary: Insurance and deficiency in service.

title: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
summary: Transgender persons are recognised as a third gender. They have the right to self-identification of their gender as male, female, or third gender. The State must provide equal opportunities in education and employment; transgenders to be treated as socially and educationally backward class for reservation purposes.

title: Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli
summary: Irretrievable breakdown of marriage should be a ground for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act. Where parties have been living separately for many years and no possibility of reunion, courts should not deny dissolution. SC recommended Parliament add irretrievable breakdown as a ground.
titleAliases: Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli

title: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
summary: Section 377 IPC to the extent it criminalises consensual same-sex conduct between adults is unconstitutional as violating Articles 14, 15, 19, and 21. Sexual orientation is an essential attribute of identity protected by right to privacy and dignity. Decriminalises homosexuality in India. Overruled Suresh Kumar Koushal.
holding: S.377 IPC criminalisation of consensual adult same-sex acts struck down; sexual orientation and gender identity are protected under Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21.

title: Neeharika Infrastructure v. State of Maharashtra
summary: High Court cannot quash FIR in exercise of writ jurisdiction when investigation pending.

title: Nikhil Mehta v. AMR Infrastructure
summary: Financial debt and home buyer claims under IBC.

title: Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa
summary: Public-law compensation is a distinct remedy available against the State under Articles 32 and 226 for custodial deaths and violations of fundamental rights. The State is liable in public law for the acts of its police officers. Compensation under this head is constitutional and does not require a civil suit; it is awarded as a solatium for the violation of fundamental rights.

title: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
summary: Right to livelihood is a facet of Article 21 right to life. Pavement dwellers evicted without adequate notice and without providing alternative accommodation would be deprived of means of livelihood, thereby violating Article 21. Reasonable notice and opportunity must be given before eviction.
titleAliases: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation

title: Olympus Superstructures v. Meena Vijay Khetan
summary: Specific performance of agreement to sell.

title: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. M/s Narbheram Power and Steel Pvt. Ltd.
summary: Arbitration clause in an insurance policy must be strictly construed. Where the policy clause expressly provides that once the insurer has disputed or not accepted liability, no difference or dispute shall be referred to arbitration, such clause bars arbitration. Parties are bound by the terms of their policy; courts cannot rewrite the clause.
holding: Arbitration clause strictly construed; insurer's express denial of liability under policy exclusion bars referral of dispute to arbitration.

title: Pioneer Urban Land v. Union of India
summary: RERA vs IBC interplay for home buyers.

title: Prasanta Kumar Sarkar v. Ashis Chatterjee
summary: The Supreme Court enumerated bail factors: nature and gravity of accusation; character, behaviour, means, and standing of the accused; circumstances peculiar to accused; prima facie satisfaction of court of commission of offence; reasonable apprehension of tampering with witnesses or threat to complainant; likelihood of fleeing justice.
holding: Bail factors: nature/gravity of accusation; character, behaviour, means, and standing of accused; prima facie satisfaction of court; reasonable apprehension of tampering with witnesses; likelihood of fleeing justice.
titleAliases: Prasanta Kumar Sarkar v. Ashis Chatterjee

title: Prem Chand Garg v. Excise Commissioner, U.P.
summary: Order under Article 142 (doing complete justice) must not be inconsistent with fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution or with substantive statutory provisions. Article 142 power is supplementary but cannot supplant the law.

title: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Gurdev Singh
summary: Reinstatement with full back wages is the normal relief for illegal termination under the Industrial Disputes Act. Employer must show valid justification for denial of back wages; employee who was not gainfully employed during the period is entitled to full back wages.
titleAliases: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Gurdev Singh

title: Raja Soap Factory v. S.P. Shantharaj
summary: SLP under Article 136 can be filed against orders of High Courts and other courts/tribunals. There is no limit on the class of cases — civil, criminal, or administrative. Concurrent findings of fact are ordinarily not disturbed in SLP unless there is perversity or miscarriage of justice.

title: Rajasthan State Road Transport v. Krishna Kant
summary: Disciplinary proceedings and domestic enquiry.

title: Rajnesh v. Neha
summary: Comprehensive guidelines on maintenance under CrPC §125 (BNSS §144 successor): maintenance must be paid from the date of application (not from the date of order); courts must direct filing of income and asset affidavits; quantum must be assessed on disclosed income and standard of living; overlapping maintenance orders in different proceedings should be consolidated.
holding: Maintenance is payable from the date of application. Courts must direct parties to file income and asset affidavits. Quantum must be assessed on disclosed income.
titleAliases: Rajnesh v. Neha

title: Rangappa v. Sri Mohan
summary: Presumption under s.139 NI Act and rebuttal standards.

title: S.M. Nilajkar v. Telecom District Manager
summary: Regularisation of daily wage workers.

title: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
summary: First Judges Case. Consultation with Chief Justice of India under Article 124 does not mean concurrence; the executive retains primacy in judicial appointments. Later overruled by Second and Third Judges cases which established Collegium system.

title: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
summary: Nine-judge bench. Laid down guidelines for Article 356 (President's Rule). Presidential proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review. Floor test must be the primary method to assess a government's majority, not the Governor's subjective assessment. Secularism is a basic feature of the Constitution.
holding: Article 356 proclamation subject to judicial review; floor test is the standard for assessing majority; secularism is basic structure.

title: Sahara India Real Estate Corporation Ltd. v. SEBI
summary: Doctrine of postponement of media publication to ensure fair trial. Open court principle is the norm; postponement is an exception requiring compelling justification. Court has inherent power to postpone publication of proceedings to protect administration of justice.

title: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh
summary: Comprehensive exposition on cruelty as a ground for divorce under §13(1)(ia) HMA. Cruelty includes mental cruelty. Enumerates circumstances constituting mental cruelty: consistent false allegations, making spouse's life a living hell, unilateral decision not to have children, sustained humiliation. Single act may or may not constitute cruelty depending on intensity.
titleAliases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh

title: Sanjay Chandra v. CBI
summary: Bail is the rule, jail is the exception. Factors to consider: nature and gravity of accusation, antecedents of the accused, possibility of flight risk, likelihood of repeating the offence, and whether releasing on bail would be prejudicial to justice. Economic offences require additional scrutiny but do not automatically exclude bail.
holding: Bail is the rule, jail is the exception.
titleAliases: Sanjay Chandra v. CBI

title: Saradamani Kandappan v. S. Rajalakshmi
summary: Refund of earnest money/advance with interest is an alternative relief when specific performance is refused. Court may grant compensation under Specific Relief Act when performance is inequitable.
holding: Refund of earnest money/advance with interest is an alternative relief when specific performance is refused. Court may grant compensation under Specific Relief Act when performance is inequitable.
titleAliases: Saradamani Kandappan v. S. Rajalakshmi

title: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI
summary: Comprehensive guidelines on bail. Courts must not impose onerous conditions. Bail conditions must be reasonable and not tantamount to refusal of bail. Prolonged incarceration without trial is a violation of right to liberty. Default bail (BNSS §187) must be granted on completion of statutory period.
holding: Comprehensive bail guidelines. No onerous conditions. Bail conditions must be reasonable. Prolonged incarceration without trial violates right to liberty. Default bail must be granted on completion of statutory period.
titleAliases: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI

title: Secretary, State of Karnataka v. Umadevi
summary: Regularisation — must follow constitutional scheme of appointment.

title: Seema Arora v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai
summary: Status quo order may be granted to preserve subject matter of suit pending adjudication. Court balances inconvenience to plaintiff against hardship to defendant when property is being alienated to third parties.
holding: Status quo order may be granted to preserve subject matter of suit pending adjudication when property is being alienated to third parties.
titleAliases: Seema Arora v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai

title: Sehgal School of Competition v. Dalbir Singh
summary: Educational institutions and CPA.

title: Selvi v. State of Karnataka
summary: Forcible administration of narco-analysis, lie-detector test, and brain-mapping violates Article 20(3) (right against self-incrimination) and Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty). Such tests amount to testimonial compulsion. Mental privacy is protected.

title: Shail Kumari Devi v. Krishan Bhagwan Pathak
summary: Maintenance pendente lite under CrPC 125.

title: Shailja v. Khobbanna
summary: Mere capability to earn does not disentitle a wife from maintenance under CrPC §125 (BNSS §144). The question is whether the wife is actually earning sufficient income to maintain herself comfortably; a theoretical earning capacity is distinct from actual income and cannot be used to deny or severely reduce maintenance.

title: Shamima Farooqui v. Shahid Khan
summary: Maintenance quantum must be sufficient for the wife to live with reasonable comfort at a standard matching her pre-separation living conditions; courts cannot fix a niggardly or token amount. Independent income or earning capacity of the wife is a factor but does not by itself disentitle her; the quantum must be fair and just. Courts must give reasons for the quantum fixed.
titleAliases: Shamima Farooqui v. Shahid Khan

title: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
summary: Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368. The word "law" in Article 13 does not include a constitutional amendment. First constitutional amendment upheld.

title: Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India
summary: Inordinate and inexplicable delay in execution of death sentence (after rejection of mercy petition) constitutes a separate ground for commutation to life imprisonment under Article 21. Overruled Devender Singh Bhullar to the extent it denied commutation on delay grounds for anti-terrorism convicts.

title: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
summary: Triple Talaq (talaq-e-biddat) declared unconstitutional as manifestly arbitrary under Article 14. Practice of instantaneous irrevocable divorce by a Muslim husband held to violate Article 14. Parliament subsequently enacted the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019.

title: Shilpa Shailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan
summary: Supreme Court can grant divorce on irretrievable breakdown under Article 142.

title: Sholay Media Entertainment v Parag Sanghvi
summary: Awarded substantial damages for copyright infringement of the film Sholay, reinforcing moral rights and commercial exploitation of cinematograph works.
holding: Copyright in a cinematograph film extends to characters, dialogues, and plot elements; infringement warrants both injunction and damages.

title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
summary: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act 2000 struck down as unconstitutional for violating Article 19(1)(a) freedom of speech and expression. The provision was vague, overbroad and not protected under Article 19(2) reasonable restrictions. Online speech cannot be curtailed on grounds of causing annoyance or being grossly offensive without clear nexus to Article 19(2) grounds.
holding: Section 66A is void as it violates Article 19(1)(a) — vague prohibitions on online speech cannot survive constitutional scrutiny.
titleAliases: Shreya Singhal v Union of India

title: Shyam Narayan Chouksey v. Union of India
summary: National anthem in cinemas — fundamental duties context.

title: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra
summary: Comprehensive guidelines on anticipatory bail under CrPC §438 (BNSS §482). Personal liberty is a cherished right. Courts must not impose blanket conditions restricting normal life. Anticipatory bail should not be time-limited as a rule; conditions must be reasonable and not onerous.
holding: Factors for anticipatory bail: nature and gravity of accusation; antecedents; possibility of fleeing justice; accusation made bona fide or with malice. Courts should not impose conditions that render anticipatory bail meaningless.
titleAliases: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra

title: Smt. Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani
summary: Limitation for suit for specific performance runs from the date fixed for performance, or if no date is fixed, from the date when plaintiff has notice that performance is refused. Agreement to sell must be proved by registered or unregistered document as applicable.
holding: Limitation for suit for specific performance runs from the date fixed for performance, or if no date is fixed, from the date when plaintiff has notice that performance is refused.
titleAliases: Smt. Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani

title: Spring Meadows Hospital v. Harjol Ahluwalia
summary: Medical negligence constitutes deficiency in service under Consumer Protection Act. Parents/guardians can file complaint on behalf of minor patients. Hospital is vicariously liable for negligence of its doctors and staff.
holding: Medical negligence constitutes deficiency in service under Consumer Protection Act. Parents/guardians can file on behalf of minors. Hospital is vicariously liable for negligence of doctors and staff.
titleAliases: Spring Meadows Hospital v. Harjol Ahluwalia

title: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction Co. Ltd. v. NHPC Ltd.
summary: Patent illegality under Section 34 means illegality apparent on the face of the award. It does not include re-appreciation of evidence. Award contrary to fundamental policy of Indian law (including constitutional principles) can be set aside under public policy ground.
titleAliases: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction Co. Ltd. v. NHPC Ltd.

title: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
summary: Categories where FIR can be quashed under inherent powers.

title: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
summary: Enumerated categories of cases where High Court can exercise jurisdiction to quash FIR/proceedings: where allegation does not constitute cognisable offence, where there is legal bar, where allegations are absurd, or where criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide intent. Often cited in criminal revision / quashing proceedings.

title: State of Karnataka v. L. Muniswamy
summary: Quashing when allegations do not disclose cognizable offence.

title: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
summary: Communal Government Order reserving seats in medical and engineering colleges in Madras based on religion and caste violated Article 15(1). Directive Principles cannot override Fundamental Rights. Led to the First Constitutional Amendment adding Article 15(4) enabling special provisions for backward classes.

title: State of Punjab v. Rafiq Masih
summary: Equal pay for equal work — daily wagers.

title: Steel Authority of India v. National Union Waterfront Workers
summary: Contract labour abolition and absorption principles.

title: Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration
summary: Habeas corpus jurisdiction extends beyond questions of initial legality of detention to conditions of custody and continuing treatment of the detainee. Courts can direct production and inquiry into custodial conditions. Right to personal liberty under Article 21 is not extinguished upon lawful arrest; residual rights survive.

title: Sunita Kachwaha v. Anil Kachwaha
summary: Income affidavits are the primary evidentiary basis for fixing maintenance quantum; the court must carefully scrutinise affidavits filed by both parties. A court that fails to consider the income affidavit on record and fixes an arbitrary amount acts contrary to the principles established by this Court. Non-consideration of material evidence constitutes a material irregularity.

title: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (Fourth Judges Case)
summary: Fourth Judges Case. National Judicial Appointments Commission Act and the 99th Constitutional Amendment struck down as unconstitutional. Collegium system restored. Primacy of CJI in judicial appointments upheld. Judicial independence forms part of the basic structure.

title: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (Second Judges Case)
summary: Second Judges Case. Overruled S.P. Gupta. Consultation under Article 124 means concurrence; the Chief Justice of India's opinion has primacy. Collegium system evolved: CJI plus two senior-most judges. Appointment cannot be made in disagreement with CJI.

title: Supreme Court Bar Association v. Union of India
summary: Article 142 powers cannot be controlled by any statutory provision, but they are not meant to be used when their exercise would directly conflict with what is expressly provided for in a statute. Article 142 is meant to supplement law, not supplant it.

title: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Haryana
summary: Sale of immovable property of value above threshold can only be effected by a registered conveyance deed, not by GPA/SA/Will transactions. GPA-based transactions are not a substitute for registered sale deed; confer no title on vendee.
holding: Sale of immovable property can only be effected by registered conveyance deed, not by GPA/SA/Will transactions. GPA-based transactions confer no title on vendee.
titleAliases: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Haryana

title: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
summary: Constitution Bench: Anticipatory bail does not have a fixed duration and continues until trial unless the court imposes time limits with reasons. Court can limit duration in exceptional circumstances. Court should not ordinarily limit duration to investigation period only.
titleAliases: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)

title: Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India
summary: IBC constitutional validity — commercial wisdom of CoC.

title: T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
summary: Eleven-judge bench. Setting up an educational institution is an "occupation" under Article 19(1)(g). Scheme in Unni Krishnan declared illegal and unconstitutional. State cannot regulate admission and fee policy of unaided private minority institutions. Some academic standards regulations permissible. Minority institutions may admit a reasonable proportion of non-minority students.

title: Tata Cellular v. Union of India
summary: Judicial review of administrative action: courts can interfere when decision is illegal, irrational, or procedurally improper. Wednesbury unreasonableness test — a decision so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have arrived at it. Merit review is not within judicial review scope.
titleAliases: Tata Cellular v. Union of India

title: Tata Sons Ltd v Greenpeace International
summary: Balanced trademark protection against freedom of expression in parody and criticism campaigns using the TATA mark.
holding: Trademark rights may be limited where use is non-commercial, descriptive, or protected speech — but dilution through tarnishment remains actionable.

title: Union Carbide Corporation v. Union of India
summary: Bhopal gas tragedy settlement. Prohibitions or limitations in ordinary law do not ipso facto operate as limitations on the constitutional power of the Supreme Court under Article 142. The Court's power to do complete justice can override procedural and substantive statutory bars when warranted in a given case.

title: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
summary: Tax treaty abuse and DTAA applicability.

title: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals
summary: GST compensation cess constitutional validity.

title: V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat
summary: Mental cruelty — subjective test.

title: Vanamala v. H.M. Ranganatha Bhatta
summary: Permanent alimony under Hindu Marriage Act.

title: Vidhya Viswanathan v. Kartik Balakrishnan
summary: Mental cruelty under §13(1)(ia) HMA. SC affirmed High Court decree of divorce on the ground of mental cruelty and awarded ₹40 lakh as permanent alimony. Decision dated 22 September 2014. This case concerns cruelty as a matrimonial ground — NOT Article 142 / irretrievable breakdown.

title: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
summary: Arbitrability of landlord-tenant disputes.

title: Vijay Kumar V. Iyer v. Infrastructure Leasing
summary: Personal guarantor insolvency under IBC.

title: Vinny Parmar v. Paramvir Parmar
summary: Maintenance under CrPC §125 (BNSS §144) is ordinarily payable from the date of application; the court has discretion to fix a date but it should not ordinarily be later than the date of filing. Delay in disposal of the case should not penalise the applicant or deprive her of arrears.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
summary: Landmark: SC laid down Vishaka Guidelines on prevention and redressal of sexual harassment of women at the workplace, pending parliamentary legislation. Sexual harassment violates Articles 14, 15, and 21. Employer has duty to provide safe workplace. Guidelines later codified in the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act 2013.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
summary: Laid down binding guidelines for prevention of sexual harassment at the workplace until legislation was enacted (later codified in the POSH Act 2013).
holding: Employers and institutions must provide a safe working environment and mechanisms to address sexual harassment complaints at the workplace.
titleAliases: Vishaka v State of Rajasthan

title: Vodafone International Holdings v. Union of India
summary: Indirect transfer — retrospective tax controversy.

title: Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate v. Management
summary: Definition of workman and industry.

title: Workmen of Meenakshi Mills Ltd. v. Meenakshi Mills Ltd.
summary: Standing orders under the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act 1946 govern the terms and conditions of employment in certified industrial establishments. Departure from certified standing orders in matters of discipline constitutes unfair labour practice.

title: Yahoo! Inc v Akash Arora
summary: Landmark cybersquatting decision holding that a domain name identical to a well-known trademark constitutes passing off and trademark infringement in India.
holding: Use of a domain name confusingly similar to a registered trademark amounts to passing off and dilution of goodwill.

title: Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. v. Mohd. Sharaful Haque
summary: Summoning standards — prima facie case required.
